newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber stable, factories shut after riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber stable, factories shut after riot.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were mostly stable in late morning trading on Monday, with some rubber factories in Banjarmasin shut for business temporarily following a fire and riot in the South Kalimantan city last Friday, traders said.
"I heard that five factories in Banjarmasin have closed temporarily following the incident and there is no buying and selling of rubber there at the moment," one trader said.
The death toll in arson and rioting in Banjarmasin had reportedly risen to 142, but Jakarta was relatively calm ahead of the May 29 general election.
The traders said August delivery SIR20 was offered at 47.50 cents/lb fob Medan, 47.25-50 cents fob Palembang and Surabaya, 46.75 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.
They said Singapore dealers had bid 47.00 cents at Medan but no deals had been done. "I think the bid is low, and there have been no deals yet," one trader said.

The traders also said demand was generally weak, with no news of interest from Chinese buyers who were reportedly looking to Indonesia following Thai government intervention-buying to prop up domestic prices. "I have not heard of any Chinese interest so far in Indonesian rubber," one trader said.
"These days, the Chinese do not buy in big volumes," the trader said. "They buy in quantities of 100 tonnes or so, so that their buying does not push up prices."
Thai traders had said their government had bought rubber from the domestic market at $1.11 a kg.

Indonesian traders said local prices were likely to stay soft this week following last week's sale of 29,651,411 lbs of technically-specified rubber by the U.S. Defence National Stockpile Centre to Intertex World Resources at prices ranging from 32.25-37.00 cents/lb.
